extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Doug Sweeny in the listing quarter to size an Official Health Technology Partner entry at Andretti Formula E against Season 13, agree an announcement window after the bell, and put a readiness pilot in front of the team's performance staff before the Austin E-Prix.

value.text: Season 13 is 21 races in 13 cities on four continents between December and July. The limiting factor for drivers, race engineers and travelling crew across that schedule is sleep debt and circadian disruption, not fitness. Oura Ring gives the team's performance staff readiness, sleep-stage, heart-rate-variability and body-temperature data per person per day - the same instrumentation Oura supplies to Team USA and supplied to Red Bull Racing's drivers and pit crew from 2020.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: Travel and training plans built on measured recovery rather than assumption; a documented readiness protocol for a double-header weekend; an early-warning signal on illness in a travelling party of dozens. In a cost-capped, weight-sensitive series, a partner whose product is consumed by the people rather than the car is one the team can adopt without engineering trade-offs.
value.label: What the team can do with it

value.text: Oura brings a five-million-member consumer base and a marketing organisation that has just spent a year activating Olympic, soccer and tennis properties. For Andretti that is retail reach, a co-branded content series on human performance in motorsport, and a partner whose brand is welcome in exactly the health-and-wellness territory Formula E's audience skews toward.
value.label: Commercial and content lift

value.text: Official Health Technology Partner designation, sidepod and race-suit placement, naming of the team's readiness programme, driver and engineer access for Oura's channels, and hospitality at the Austin E-Prix and the Miami E-Prix for Oura's retail partners and new public-market investors.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: Oura Inc. filed a public Form S-1 with the SEC on 3 September 2026 for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker OURA. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Allen & Company and Jefferies lead the offering, with around a dozen further banks named. A confidential draft was submitted on 21 May 2026; this is the public step, and it is the reason the company is in front of every institutional investor in the country this month.
why_now.label: The trigger

why_now.text: Revenue of $1.21B for the nine months to 30 June 2026, up 74% from $697.6M a year earlier. Trailing-twelve-month revenue of $1.4B at $59M of net profit. Five million paid members against 2.5 million a year earlier, and 3.6 million rings sold over twelve months. The nine-month loss attributable to common stockholders of $924.3M is an accounting artefact of a $985.0M deemed dividend to preferred holders, not trading performance.
why_now.label: The numbers the filing put on the record

why_now.text: The Series E in October 2025 raised more than $900M at an $11B valuation, led by Fidelity with ICONIQ, Whale Rock and Atreides - double the $5B set at the Series D in December 2024. TechCrunch reported on 24 August that the listing could value Oura above $16B. That figure is reported, not confirmed, and no price range is set in the filing.
why_now.label: The re-pricing

why_now.text: Formula E opens Season 13 at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026 and runs 21 races across 13 cities to July 2027. Teams close Season 13 partner rosters through the autumn. A deal agreed in the listing quarter can be announced after the bell and activated for the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027 and the Miami E-Prix two weeks later.
why_now.label: The calendar

why_team.text: The sponsor table shows no wearable, health-technology or recovery partner on any 2026 Formula E roster. On the Formula 1 grid the same lane is filling fast - WHOOP at Scuderia Ferrari, Eight Sleep at Aston Martin Aramco. Official Health Technology Partner is therefore available in Formula E as a clean, ownable designation rather than a contested one.
why_team.label: An empty category across a whole championship

why_team.text: Andretti Formula E is the US team on the grid, run under TWG Global with TWG AI as primary partner of the Formula E programme and Official Artificial Intelligence Partner of Andretti Global since 2026, alongside Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo. Season 13 gives it two home rounds, Austin and Miami, which is where a newly Nasdaq-listed consumer brand wants its hospitality.
why_team.label: The American entry, for an American listing

why_team.text: Oura is Official Wearable of Team USA and the LA28 Games and of U.S. Soccer's 27 national teams, and holds a five-year USTA agreement covering the US Open. A three-year Formula E term running to LA28 is the same audience and the same message, extended to the one arena the shelf is missing.
why_team.label: It sits inside the portfolio Oura already owns

why_team.text: Three reasons, stated plainly. The Formula 1 human-performance lane is taken at the two teams that fit. Oura's own Formula 1 history sits at Red Bull Racing, which is not on its 2026 roster, so a return means re-opening a lapsed relationship or partnering a direct rival of it. And Formula E's price for a category-defining designation is a fraction of Formula 1's, which matters in the first budget cycle after a listing.
why_team.label: Why Formula E and not Formula 1

ruled_out.reason: WHOOP has joined the roster - a direct wearable rival in the same recovery category.
Eight Sleep has joined the roster; sleep and recovery is the same lane Oura would buy.
Oura's own 2020 Official Health Technology partnership ran here and does not appear on the 2026 roster; returning means re-opening a lapsed deal, and TAG Heuer holds the worn-device territory.
Optimum Nutrition occupies the athlete-performance lane on the roster.
Open on health, but Chase locks financial services and the technology story runs through TCS; no US home round to activate.
Title rights are open but priced as title rights, and TDK holds the official technology designation after TAG Heuer's exit.
Genuinely open, but a works OEM entry whose Season 13 story is Tokyo; it gives a US-listing consumer brand no home-round identity.
Both open, but their partner narratives are sustainability and the India market rather than consumer health in the United States.

ruled_out.team: Cupra Kiro · DS Penske · Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team · Citroën Racing
ruled_out.reason: Open but OEM-fronted; the consumer-brand voice would sit behind a car marque rather than beside it.

brief_data.bottom_line: A public S-1 on 3 September, $1.4B of trailing revenue and a reported listing above $16B put Oura at the point where a newly listed consumer brand writes its next marketing plan. It has bought Team USA, U.S. Soccer and the US Open and owns nothing in motorsport, and no Formula E team carries a wearable partner.

brief_data.industry_meta: Consumer Health Technology · Smart Ring / Recovery Data
brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. Season 13 runs 21 races in 13 cities; what limits drivers, engineers and travelling crew across it is circadian, not physical. Oura Ring puts readiness, sleep and heart-rate-variability data in front of the team's performance staff - the programme it runs for Team USA and ran for Red Bull Racing's pit crew from 2020. In return: Official Health Technology Partner status, livery and race-suit presence, US-round hospitality.
brief_data.why_team_para: The sponsor table shows no wearable or health-technology partner anywhere on the 2026 Formula E grid: the designation is open across the series, at Formula E prices rather than Formula 1 ones. Andretti Formula E is the American entry, owned by TWG Global. Its roster runs TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo. Season 13 gives it two home rounds, in Austin and Miami, inside the LA28 build-up Oura has already bought.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Health Technology Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, carrying through to the LA28 Games. Estimated $2-4M a year, part-payable in product. Scope: sidepod and race-suit placement, naming of the team's readiness programme, US-round hospitality, performance content.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The S-1 went public on 3 September and pricing follows within weeks; a newly listed company sets its marketing plan in the first cycle after the bell. Formula E opens Season 13 at the Jeddah E-Prix in December, and the Austin E-Prix and the Miami E-Prix land in February 2027.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Sweeny owns the sports portfolio that bought Team USA, U.S. Soccer and the US Open; he came from Levi's, Nest and One Medical. Path: Tom Hale, chief executive since March 2022, who took Momentive public in 2018, and Sean Brecker, CFO. No president is listed.
brief_data.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the listing, not the ring.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Doug, you own Team USA, U.S. Soccer and the US Open, and nothing in motorsport. No Formula E team carries a wearable partner, and Andretti runs the Austin E-Prix and the Miami E-Prix before LA28. 25 minutes?”
